notify_on: Any centralized exchange (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, OKX, Bybit, KuCoin, MEXC, Gate.io, Bitget, Upbit, etc.) announcing a FRINK/FRNK/Frinkcoin spot or futures listing
A confirmed new DEX pool for a FRINK-named token on a new chain
The Frink Coin presale token completing its planned DEX listing
do_not_notify_on: Aggregator pages merely restating the unverified Kraken/Figure/BYDFi venue claims
Price movement with no listing event
Presale marketing or 'top memecoin' listicles with no listing event

CRITICAL FALSE POSITIVE: exchange 'price pages' (coinbase.com/price/..., bitget.com/price/..., binance.com/price/...). These exist for thousands of assets the exchange does NOT list for trading and are auto-generated. A price page is NEVER evidence of a listing. Only a dated announcement from the exchange's own newsroom/announcements feed counts.

Inflated market-cap figures on aggregator pages (e.g. Bitget showing FRNK at $0.006804 / $142.89M mcap) that contradict $0 24h volume elsewhere. Market cap = price x supply and is meaningless without liquidity; a dead token can show a large mcap. Not a listing signal.

CRITICAL FALSE POSITIVE: DEX aggregators, routers, wallets and trading bots (Jupiter, Phantom, Maestro Bot, Soul Sniper, MEXC DEX+, 1inch etc.) 'supporting' a token. These surface ANY token with an on-chain pool automatically - they are not listings and involve no exchange decision. 'MEXC DEX+' in particular is MEXC's on-chain aggregator front-end and is NOT a MEXC centralized-exchange listing.
baseline_notes: 2026-09-09 00:48Z check: no listing. Recorded a sixth Ethereum FRINK (0x57fe4fdb..., deployed ~Oct 2024) confirmed directly from Etherscan via user screenshot - unindexed by every aggregator, deployer bridge-funded.
data_quality_warnings: Bitget reports FRNK at $0.006804 with a $142.89M market cap while CoinMarketCap/CoinCarp report the token untracked with $0 volume. The Bitget figure is almost certainly price x total supply on a token with no real market. Do not treat it as a valuation.

Bitget's web3 swap page for FRNK (web3.bitget.com/en/swap/bnb/0xf938c9A2...) labels the chain as BNB while using the ETHEREUM contract address. Aggregators mismatch chain and contract for this ticker - another reason to verify on a block explorer rather than trusting aggregator pages.

DEXTools /pair-explorer/<addr> URLs expose PAIR addresses, not token contracts. Coinscan /tokens/eth/<addr> implies a token. The same address (0x8082db21...) appears under both, so at least one aggregator is mislabelling. Without explorer access this cannot be resolved - never present an address whose type is unresolved as a token contract.

Search summaries conflate FRNK 0xf938c9a2 (21M supply, 29 holders, no pool) with FRINKCOIN 0x46493b80 (1B supply, 461 holders, ~$3.3K pool). Liquidity figures attributed to 'Frinkcoin' usually belong to the latter. Always attribute market data to a specific contract.

2026-09-09: a search summary reported '$0.00 24h volume, $2.67K market cap, 1 billion circulating supply' for 0xed2ee398. That was CONFLATION - the 1B supply belongs to 0x46493b80. Direct verification showed 0xed2ee398 stable at ~$10.8K liquidity and ~$8.7K volume. Always re-verify alarming metrics against a second query before acting on them.

episode_timeline.premise_made_public: January 2020 - Fox released the episode title and synopsis; covered by The Springfield Shopper (news.simpsonswiki.com) in Jan 2020 under 'Professor Frink develops a cryptocurrency that makes him rich in February'
episode_timeline.earliest_known_FRINK_token: FRNK 0xf938c9a2... - 'February 2020', day-level precision unavailable from search; Etherscan verification 2020-04-12
episode_timeline.conclusion: NO FRINK-named token is known to predate the episode. Even if FRNK were minted 1-22 Feb 2020 (before broadcast), the premise was already public from January 2020, so it could not constitute foreknowledge or prediction. Every FRINK token post-dates public knowledge of the episode.

frink_language_founder_watch.subject: Alan Eliasen - designer and implementer of the Frink programming language (frinklang.org), first released Dec 2001. Also authored several faster BigInteger algorithms in Java 8.
frink_language_founder_watch.naming_link: Eliasen named the LANGUAGE after Professor Frink from The Simpsons - the same character the episode's fictional coin is named for. So the language and the memecoins share a source, not a lineage.
frink_language_founder_watch.finding_20260911: NO EVIDENCE that Alan Eliasen has launched, endorsed, or been involved with any cryptocurrency. Multiple searches across his name, the language, and crypto/blockchain terms returned only his programming-language work. No token names him as founder.
frink_language_founder_watch.no_disclaimer_found: Could not locate any statement on frinklang.org either claiming or disclaiming affiliation with any FRINK token.
frink_language_founder_watch.caution: Absence of evidence from web search is not proof. But the pattern here is the opposite of a founder launch: tokens borrowing a name, with no named team.
